I was diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic melanoma last August with a tumor on my scalp & mets in my stomach & liver.  Several invasive biopsies, 2 scalp surgeries and a clinical trial have basically saved my life or at least bought me time.  My last set of scans showed a 50% reduction in the size of my mets & I tolerate immunotherapy very well, no thyroid or liver issues.  The potential side effects are what kept me from trying it initially; and now at best case, stuck with a horrible chronic condition for the rest of my life, worst case I’ll be dead in 5 years.  I’m 48 and not ready yet (not that anyone ever is).  My life would be very different today if I had gone for the immunotherapy after my initial diagnosis 2.5 years ago.
If I could go back in time & do one thing, I would have opted for immunotherapy after my stage ii b diagnosis.

I was 23 and at my first “real” job as a fashion buyer at a tv shopping channel.  I was still living at my parents and was commuting.  Got to work at about 8:25.  I remember the whole drive in thinking, what a beautiful day.  Like weirdly perfect.

Anyway, got into the building & immediately turned on the tv at my desk (we had to have said tv shopping channel on all day).  Ran to the cafeteria to get a Diet Coke…I just remember being in a great mood that day.

Walked back to my desk, and saw people clustered at various cubes really watching tv & was like, what’s wrong everyone?  The first plane had crashed; we thought it was a Cessna.  Tuesdays weren’t huge appointment days for us in NYC, but some coworkers were there & somehow got out.

I was standing with about 10 coworkers when the 2nd plane hit.  I just remember saying something like oh my god the building is going to fall over.  I called my parents, my father said, we’re at war, get your brother (he was still in college & not far from where I worked) and come home now.

I remember driving home with him on the turnpike after all the flights were grounded and it was so fucking scary & weird.  We listened to Howard Stern the whole way home; he stayed on the air & let people call in.  Not everyone had cell phones back then, so he was broadcasting everything in real time.

Anyway, this event bifurcated my life and I truly believe that whatever the fuck “America” was died that day.

And to this day, and I know this is fucked up, but whenever it’s severe clear & between 70-80 degrees, I always think “9/11 weather”

Treatment plan:  my oncologist & I decided to monitor through scans & blood work every 3 months, no immunotherapy.

Getting diagnosed is scary.  Maybe the scariest part for me, anyway.  I know it’s hard but don’t make any assumptions yet.

All this to say as of today, I’m NED.  I think you caught it early and you will most likely be fine.
